Bitcoin slips back to $60,000 as US open triggers long liquidations

A morning bounce above $62,000 unwound within an hour of Wall Street's reopening, even as technology stocks rallied.

Bitcoin fell from about $61,400 to a low of $58,729 on Kraken in the hour after US markets opened at 14:30 UK on Friday, according to Kraken data, and traded near $60,000 at 16:30 UK.

About $190 million of positions were forced shut in the hour of the drop, $182 million of them bets on rising prices, TokenPost reported. Ether fell about 4% to near $1,660 over the same hour.

The fall came as US stocks reopened higher after Thanksgiving. The Nasdaq 100 was up nearly 2% by late morning in New York, though Nvidia fell more than 2%, CoinDesk reported. No single crypto-specific trigger was reported.

The low stayed just above $58,525, the level at which Galaxy Digital said a daily close would mark 'the start of a move to a materially lower low'. In a report this week Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market ended in June, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Glassnode said buy orders cluster between $50,000 and $58,000, according to CoinDesk.

Zcash fell from about $760 to $710 in the same move and recovered to near $739, still up on the day. US markets close early at 18:00 UK, and bitcoin is on course for its first weekly gain in eight weeks if it holds until Sunday's close, CoinDesk reported.

Bitcoin gave up its morning bounce at the US open, falling to $58,729 before steadying near $60,000 as about $190 million of longs were liquidated. The low stayed just above Galaxy's $58,525 warning level.

item.title: Fri 27 Nov 06:35 · mixed · Bitcoin climbs back above $61,000 before monthly options expiry
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Bitcoin climbed overnight to about $61,680 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, roughly $800 above the evening edition, with most of the gain in a jump around 02:00 UK; the overnight high was $61,925.
  2. Zcash rose about 5% to near $758 on Kraken, as KuCoin said it will delist Monero on 30 November and Grayscale said its Zcash commitment will last 'many years', Cointelegraph reported.
  3. Binance said withdrawals are fully restored four weeks after the $6.3 billion October hack, CoinDesk reported.

What changed: A little firmer than the evening. Bitcoin pushed back above $61,000 in thin Asian holiday trade, and ZEC recovered most of Thursday's drop. US stocks close early at 18:00 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Bitcoin climbs back above $61,000 before monthly options expiry

Bitcoin rose about $800 overnight in thin holiday trade, while Zcash gained 5% as a rival privacy coin lost another exchange listing.

Bitcoin traded near $61,680 on Kraken at 06:30 UK on Friday, up about $800 from the previous evening, after a jump at around 02:00 UK took it to an overnight high of $61,925, according to Kraken data.

The move came with US markets shut for Thanksgiving and Asian volumes light, and FXStreet described it as a tentative rebound. About $7 billion of bitcoin options expire on Deribit at 08:00 UK, which traders have watched for a pull towards $60,000, where puts cluster.

Zcash rose about 5% to near $758, recovering most of Thursday's fall. KuCoin said it will delist Monero on 30 November and close withdrawals on 31 December, Cointelegraph reported, citing the EU's ban on anonymity-enhancing coins at regulated firms from July 2027. Grayscale's head of research, Zach Pandl, said the firm's commitment to Zcash would continue 'for many years to come'.

Separately, Binance said its withdrawal suspension from the 29 October hack had been fully lifted, CoinDesk reported. The exchange said in early November it had restored 98% of the $6.34 billion affected.

In the UK, Coinbase's European policy head Katie Harries said the FCA was 'getting its approach to DeFi wrong', Cointelegraph reported. FCA final guidance is expected in January. US stock markets reopen for a half-day session closing at 18:00 UK.

Bitcoin rose about $800 overnight to near $61,700 in thin holiday trade, ahead of this morning's $7 billion options expiry. Zcash gained 5% as KuCoin moved to drop Monero and Grayscale backed Zcash.

Cointelegraph Kraken

It removes one overhang for the biggest exchange, though the hack still shapes regulators' views. CoinDesk Cointelegraph

Coinbase's European policy head Katie Harries said the FCA's plans are 'a ban on giving [UK consumers] a regulated route' to DeFi, Cointelegraph reported. A routine pre-release, not a network upgrade; node operators would normally wait for the full release. Zcash Foundation (GitHub)

item.title: Thu 26 Nov 21:35 · mixed · JPMorgan sees bitcoin capitulation as Strategy discount hits record
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Bitcoin edged up to about $60,870 on Kraken by 21:30 UK, roughly $490 above the afternoon edition and about 0.8% up on the UTC day, in thin Thanksgiving trade.
  2. JPMorgan said Strategy's share price fell to a record low of about 0.88 times the value of its bitcoin, which it called a sign of capitulation, The Block reported.
  3. Glassnode data showed 68.5% of bitcoin has not moved for at least a year, up from 62% in July, a pattern seen in past bear-market bottoming phases, CoinDesk reported.

What changed: Slightly calmer than the afternoon. Bitcoin and ZEC both recovered a little, with ZEC back near $721 from $698. The new evening stories are capitulation and long-term holding signals that read as possible bottoming, set against a death cross on the daily chart and warnings about a hawkish Fed. Next to watch: Monthly BTC options expiry on Deribit, Friday 27 November at 08:00 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

JPMorgan sees bitcoin capitulation as Strategy discount hits record

Shares in Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, briefly traded at a record discount to its bitcoin, which JPMorgan called a sign of capitulation, The Block reported.

JPMorgan said on Wednesday that Strategy's premium to the value of its bitcoin had fallen to about 0.88 times, a record low and below the late-June trough, which it described as a sign of bitcoin capitulation, The Block reported.

Strategy's own dashboard showed the ratio at 0.88 on Wednesday morning in New York before it recovered to 0.94. JPMorgan also noted that BlackRock's IBIT fund kept losing money even during the brief price recovery, and put bitcoin's estimated production cost at about $86,000.

A separate on-chain reading pointed the same way. The share of bitcoin that has not moved for at least a year rose to 68.5%, from 62% in July, according to Glassnode data reported by CoinDesk. Similar rises came before past bear-market bottoms, though they gave little guide to timing.

Not every signal agreed. Bitcoin's 50-day average crossed below its 200-day average, a so-called death cross, Decrypt reported. Economist Robin Brooks warned of a possible 'meltdown' in risk assets before the Fed meets on 8 and 9 December, Cointelegraph reported, with FedWatch showing almost no chance of rates staying on hold.

Bitcoin traded near $60,870 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, up from about $60,380 at the afternoon edition, with US markets shut for Thanksgiving. Zcash recovered to near $721 from $698. About $7 billion of bitcoin options expire on Deribit at 08:00 UK on Friday.

JPMorgan called Strategy's record-low share discount a sign of bitcoin capitulation, while long-held supply rose to 68.5%. Bitcoin edged up to about $60,900 in holiday trade ahead of Friday's $7 billion options expiry.

JPMorgan said Strategy's market value fell to about 0.88 times its bitcoin holdings, a record low below June's, which it called a sign of capitulation; Strategy's dashboard later showed 0.94, The Block reported. The bank also noted IBIT outflows during the rebound and a production cost estimate near $86,000. The Block

The share of bitcoin unmoved for a year or more rose to 68.5% from 62% in July, per Glassnode data reported by CoinDesk. Similar rises came before past bear-market bottoms, though without a reliable guide to timing. CoinDesk
  4. 🟠 Developing The Big Picture: Fed blackout starts Saturday with a hike all but priced (Medium confidence). CME FedWatch gave only 0.5% odds of rates holding at 3.75% to 4% on 9 December, and economist Robin Brooks warned risk assets could face a 'meltdown' before the meeting if the Fed stays hawkish, Cointelegraph reported. Fed officials go quiet from 28 November, so there will be fewer speeches to shift expectations. Cointelegraph

Kraken showed ZEC near $721 at 21:30 UK, up from about $698 at the afternoon edition but still about 6% down on the UTC day from $770. No Zcash-specific trigger appeared in the inbox or Zcash forum this evening, which fits the afternoon's read of a leverage flush. Kraken

Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail showed a payment costing under 35 cents can make a wallet's rebroadcast reveal the IP address of the node watching it, working 30 out of 30 times on a test network, CoinDesk reported. Bitcoin Core and wallets built on it are affected; a fix is proposed but unreleased. A privacy issue, not a risk to funds. CoinDesk

Spain's financial intelligence unit can now freeze crypto accounts for up to five working days without a court order, under a decree that takes effect in two months, Decrypt reported. Decrypt Cointelegraph

item.title: Thu 26 Nov 16:35 · risk-off · Galaxy withdraws bitcoin bottom call as ETF exodus hits record
item.description:

  2. ZEC fell about 8% since the morning edition to near $698 on Kraken, the weakest large coin today, with long liquidations driving a sharp drop around 14:50 UK, TokenPost reported.
  3. US spot bitcoin ETF outflows for November reached $5.39 billion, already the worst month since the funds launched, The Block and CoinDesk reported.

What changed: Bitcoin is little changed at about $60,380, roughly $210 below the morning edition, in thin Thanksgiving trade. Galaxy withdraws bitcoin bottom call as ETF exodus hits record

Galaxy Research has abandoned its view that bitcoin's bear market ended in June, Decrypt reported, as November's ETF outflows passed $5 billion, the worst month on record.

Galaxy Research withdrew its October call that bitcoin's bear market had ended in June, after the signal behind it failed, Decrypt reported on Thursday.

The firm said a daily close below the 30 June closing low of $58,525 would signal a move to a materially lower low. It noted that earlier breaks of a standing bear-market low went at least 17% further, which would imply about $48,500. Bitcoin set an intraday low of $55,100 on 21 November.

The reversal came as US spot bitcoin ETFs logged $5.39 billion of net outflows so far in November, above the previous record of $4.51 billion set in June, according to SoSoValue data reported by CoinDesk. The Block reported a seventh straight day of outflows on Wednesday.

Macro pressure added to the gloom. Core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% in October, above forecasts, and CME FedWatch showed a 94% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 December, Cointelegraph reported.

Zcash was the weakest large token. ZEC fell about 8% from the morning to near $698 on Kraken, with TokenPost reporting $910,000 of long liquidations in an hour.

Bitcoin traded near $60,380 on Kraken at 16:30 UK. About $7 billion of bitcoin options expire on Deribit on Friday, with large put positions at $60,000 and below, CoinDesk reported.

Galaxy Research withdrew its call that bitcoin's bear market was over, as November ETF outflows hit a record $5.39 billion. Bitcoin is flat near $60,400 in holiday trade, while ZEC fell about 8%.

ETF selling runs to seven days even as bitcoin holds $60,000

Big US bitcoin funds lost another $453 million on Wednesday, Farside data showed, though the price kept its rebound overnight in quiet holiday trade.

US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded net outflows of $453 million on Wednesday, the seventh trading day in a row of withdrawals, according to Farside Investors data reported by JBizNews and Bloomingbit.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for about $330 million of the total. Grayscale's Bitcoin Mini Trust lost about $60 million, and Bitwise, ARK, Grayscale's GBTC, VanEck and Fidelity funds also saw money leave. Tuesday's outflow was about $231 million.

The selling came on the day bitcoin rallied nearly $3,000 from its low as US shares recovered from a morning drop, with the Dow ending in positive territory, Yahoo Finance reported.

Bitcoin held that rebound overnight. Kraken showed it touching about $61,530 around midnight UK and trading near $60,590 at 06:30 UK. Zcash was little changed near $758.

In the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority plans to proceed with authorisation requirements for decentralised finance platforms, the Financial Times reported, citing the use of DeFi protocols to move funds stolen in October's $6.3 billion Binance hack.

US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen for a half day on Friday, when monthly bitcoin options expire at 08:00 UK.

Bitcoin retakes $60,000 as Wall Street claws back early losses

A late recovery in US shares lifted bitcoin nearly $3,000 from its morning low, though analysts warned that the month remains its worst in over four years.

Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 on Wednesday afternoon in New York, turning positive for the day after rallying nearly $3,000 from its session low, CoinDesk reported. Kraken showed it near $60,260 at 21:30 UK, against a low of about $57,210.

The move tracked a recovery in US stocks. The Nasdaq, down about 4% at the open after hotter-than-expected core PCE inflation and new US tariff proposals, was down less than 1% late in the session, while the Dow turned positive, Yahoo Finance reported. The ten-year Treasury yield fell to 4.82% as investors bought bonds.

CoinDesk noted that investor Michael Burry said he had covered his technology shorts, which traders read as a sign of how stretched the selling had become.

Zcash rebounded more sharply, with ZEC near $761 on Kraken, up about 10% since the afternoon.

The wider picture stayed weak. Bitcoin was down about 24% in November, its worst month since June 2022, CoinDesk reported. Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market had ended and said a daily close below $58,525 would point to lower lows.

US markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen for a half day on Friday, when monthly bitcoin options expire.

Bitcoin rallied back above $60,000 as US stocks recovered most of their early losses, and ZEC bounced about 10%. November is still on course to be bitcoin's worst month since 2022.
